title: A source claim identifies the actual distributed entry point
question: A source module and the package entry point can differ at the same commit. Record each file/symbol and verify the actual observation path.

evidence.title: Source and distributed entry points can expose different numeric boundaries
explanation: At the pinned Dintero edition, TypeScript locale formatting chooses an exact-string-capable Intl path while the package-main JavaScript path always calls its guarded toNumber conversion first.

The source branch and distributed body differ, and package.json selects dist/index.js. This is attributable artifact-path evidence; neither package publication contents nor a deployed Intl implementation was executed, and Core does not prescribe a package entry-point policy.

The relevant engine must support exact decimal-string Intl formatting for the TypeScript branch to avoid native-number conversion; otherwise both routes use the guarded conversion. An exact stored amount beyond native-number round-trip precision can hit the JavaScript conversion error path before formatting; the TypeScript capability branch may avoid it. This is a conditional source trace, not an observed installed-package result. This behavior is not currently defined by FinKore Core.

explanation: Generated MoneyPHP/Teller factories share dynamic dispatch and do not verify generated aliases against metadata at dispatch; Teller constructs ISO metadata even for documentary non-ISO method names.

explanation: Dinero documentary nondecimal formatters filter zero components before applying denomination labels, losing positional meaning; a separate percentage example passes an unused third allocate argument.
